To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PTC124, an FDA-approved drug, directly inhibits firefly luciferases, and that this inhibition is responsible for the initial discovery of the compound as an activator of nonsense codon readthrough in a FLuc cell-based assay.
PTC124 and related compounds are FLuc inhibitors, and this activity may have contributed to the initial identification of these compounds as nonsense codon suppressors.
the activity of PTC124 as a nonsense codon suppressor was likely biased by a direct effect on the reporter enzyme, firefly luciferas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which PTC124, originally identified as a nonsense codon suppressor, inhibits FLuc reporter activity.
the identification of the molecular targets of PTC124, which is an orally available drug that was developed to correct the genetic defects in the human disease cystic fibrosis.
the development of novel, efficient and environmentally friendly methods for the synthesis of oxadiazole derivatives and their evaluation as inhibitors of luciferase enzymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PTC124 does not inhibit nonsense-mediated mRNA decay in the presence of FLuc, but it does inhibit the luciferase enzyme.
the FLuc reporter enzyme is a direct molecular target of PPTC124 and that PTC124 does not show any nonsense suppression activity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
compounds with a specific chemical motif (3,5-diaryloxadiazoles) are FLuc inhibitors and that PTC124 is a FLuc inhibitor that also inhibits nonsense mediated decay (NMD) of luciferase mRNA.

the FLuc reporter was used in the original PTC124 HTS screen and that the PTC124 activity observed was due to direct inhibition of the luciferase enzyme and not due to the intended nonsense suppression activity of PTC124.

The main takeaway from our work is that

compounds can have direct effects on the reporter enzyme that are not related to their target activity and that these effects should be considered when interpreting HTS results and when evaluating the activity of compounds identified from HTS campaigns.
compounds that directly affect luciferase activity can be misidentified in HTS assays as having a biological effect.
the FLuc reporter is not suitable for use in HTS assays for compounds with the structural motif 3,5-diphenyl-oxadiazoles.
